mechanism_narrative: A lower current level of the federal funds rate is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuations and increase the attractiveness of equities relative to bonds.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 3%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically leads to a reduction in consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY) and a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%) signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases real interest rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5% and FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) relative to the previous quarter signals weakening demand for residential construction, which often precedes a slowdown in overall economic activity and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in HOUST is followed by positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) relative to the previous month signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO declines, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in housing starts below 2100 thousand units signals weak demand for new homes, which often indicates broader consumer weakness and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 2100.0, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) below 132,000 thousand and a rise in retail sales (RSAFS) above 350,000 million dollars signals a labor market contraction that is not fully offset by strong consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS is below 132,000 and RSAFS is above 350,000, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns due to increased real interest rates and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a rise in FEDFUNDS is followed by positive 5-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.
